Subject: Re: Question on blended billing for mixed-context sessions — worked example

Hi all — I pulled together the math against the sample lines Rachel sent. A few implementation notes first, then a concrete example.

Policy summary (how billing works today):
- Billing unit: tokens are metered per request (prompt tokens + generated tokens) at the call boundary.
- Aggregation window: minimums and certain rounding are applied per active "session" (we define an active session as a sequence of requests on the same connection with <5 minutes idle).
- Rounding quantum: for mixed workloads we apply a 16-token billing quantum on prompt-side accounting and an 8-token quantum on generated tokens.
- KV/prefix caching: first request that includes a large static context is billed fully; subsequent requests in the same session use cached prefix benefits which reduce billed prompt tokens (we report both raw and net billed tokens).

Worked example (based on your trace):
Request A (initial seed) — includes system context blob: 2,400 prompt tokens + 780 model tokens generated -> raw tokens = 3,180.
Billed: prompt rounded up to nearest 16 -> ceil(2400/16)*16 = 2,400 (already aligned) ; generated rounded up to nearest 8 -> ceil(780/8)*8 = 784.
Billed tokens for Request A = 2,400 + 784 = 3,184.

Request B (immediate follow-up, same session) — user message 120 tokens + model 220 tokens generated; prefix cached reduces context cost to 40 prompt tokens.
Billed: prompt -> ceil(40/16)*16 = 48; generated -> ceil(220/8)*8 = 224.
Billed tokens for Request B = 48 + 224 = 272.

Invoice mapping: we aggregate bills per-session for the purposes of the monthly minimum. So the two requests above would show line items (Request A: 3,184 tokens; Request B: 272 tokens) and the session-level aggregation would sum to 3,456 tokens. If your monthly committed minimum is applied per-session, the full session total is compared to the per-session minimum rather than each request independently.

Edge cases to watch for:
- Short idle spikes: if your integration reconnects after >5 minutes, we treat it as a new session and billing quantum applies again (so a large context will bill fully again).
- Streaming vs non-streamed responses: streaming can sometimes show more granular generated-token rounding; we convert stream fragments into a single generated-token total for billing.

I can produce a line-by-line CSV using your trace and the exact invoice rates so you can see dollars per line. If you want the rounding behavior to be different under a committed contract (e.g., larger quantum waived, or session aggregation window extended), that is negotiable — pinging Neha for commercial exceptions.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
